title: Version one sync: the revision, events joined by id, the same record changed on two devices asked, the one-device checks after a sync as questions (AQ1 to AQ4, AP1 to AP7; AW1 to AW7)
written_in: SCHEMA_V3 0 and 2.3; DECISIONS_ROUND2 AP and AQ (AQ wins); DECISIONS.md "Phone and desktop in version one" (Mako, 23 Nov)
notes: Every amount is made up and in whole minor units (yen). Every id has the ordinary form or a built form, as the app writes them.

A device keeps the copy it last synced (`base`) and its revision (`baseRev`). Question `push`: the vault accepts a write only on the latest revision [AQ1]. `sync_device`: a device takes the latest first when behind, joins it with its own, and writes. `cas_story`: devices sync in turn. `sync`: the join of two copies on their common base: a record or field value changed on one side only is taken; changed on both to the same content (apart from `at`, `by`, `told`, `held`, `goneBy`, and `gone` read as yes or no) is one record, the newer, with the earliest `told`; changed on both to different content is asked: the newer shows meanwhile (`at`, then `gone`, then `by`, then the text), every version is kept in `keptVersions` as `kept:<record id or field path>` with `ask: true` [AQ3]. A field value of `home`, `ui`, `plan.limits` or `imports.cats` is one item; a list record is one item whole (its rules, steps and keyed overrides with it).

Question `sync_check`: the join, then the one-device checks [AQ4] as questions (`x8`, `closed`, `minimum`, `shares`, and `which` for each kept record waiting) and notices (`reopened`, AP1). `answer` picks a kept version; `answer_check` answers a check question and lists what is still asked.
Merging rules of D4 to AP5 that are about merging (per key `at` merging, holds, AN2 and AN6 after a merge) are stage 2: their mg cases keep passing against merge_ref.js (STAGE2_MERGE_LIST.md) [AQ5].
[AW7] The shared list of kept versions is `keptVersions` (SCHEMA 2.1); the IndexedDB store keeps the name `kept`. A question's `kept` names the kept record.

cases.question: push
cases.title: AQ1: a write based on the latest revision is accepted and the revision goes up by one
cases.why: The vault holds revision 7 and the phone last took revision 7, so its write is based on the latest: accepted, and the cloud copy is now revision 7 + 1 = 8 [AQ1].

cases.question: push
cases.title: AQ1: a write based on an older revision is refused; the device must take the latest first
cases.why: The desktop wrote revision 8 after the phone last took revision 7. The phone's write is based on 7, not 8: refused, and the vault says the latest is 8 [AQ1]. Nothing in the cloud copy changes.

cases.question: sync_device
cases.title: AQ1: a device that is behind and has its own change takes the latest, joins it with its own, then writes
cases.why: Behind (7 against 8): the phone takes revision 8 first. Rent changed only on the phone (the cloud's is the one it last took), so the phone's stays; the desktop's 1,200 lunch is new and joins. The joined copy is written on 8: accepted, revision 9 [AQ1, AQ2].

cases.question: sync_device
cases.title: AQ1: a device that is behind with nothing of its own takes the latest and writes nothing
cases.why: The phone changed nothing since revision 7; the desktop renamed rent in 8. The phone takes 8 as it is; there is nothing of its own to write, so the revision stays 8.

cases.question: sync_device
cases.title: AQ1: a device on the latest revision writes its change with no join
cases.why: The phone last took 8 and the cloud is still at 8: its write is accepted as it is, revision 9.

cases.question: cas_story
cases.title: AQ1: both devices write from the same revision; the second is refused, joins and writes; both end with one copy
cases.why: The phone writes first on 5: revision 6. The desktop's write on 5 is refused; it takes 6, joins (rent from the phone, its lunch), writes on 6: revision 7. The phone then takes 7 and has nothing new: both devices hold revision 7, the same copy [AQ1].

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ2: spends typed on two devices join by id: both are kept
cases.why: Two spends with their own ordinary ids, one from each device: money that happened joins on its own, nothing is asked [AQ2]. (If they are the same lunch, the possible-double offer of 6.4 asks on one device, as before.)

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ2, O2: the same pay ticked on both devices is one record: the newer `at`, the earliest `told`
cases.why: Both write `set:<pay>@2026-12-25` with the same amount: one id, the same content apart from when and by whom, so one record and no question. The desktop's `at` (21:00) is newer; `told` stays the first heard, 19:00 [H1, O2, AQ2].

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ2, AQ3: the same pay ticked with two different amounts asks which; the other is kept
cases.why: One occurrence ticked as 250,000 on the phone and 248,000 on the desktop: the same record changed on both to different content. Shown until answered: the newer (desktop, 21:00); both versions kept in `kept:set:...`, asked [AQ3]. Nothing is lost either way. (AQ says only plan and settings records ask; an event with one id changed two ways is read the same way here: see the report's question 1.)

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ2, X1: a record the move wrote on both devices from one 38.31 copy is one record
cases.why: Both devices moved the same 38.31 receipt: `mv:rc:r1700000000123`, the copy's last save as `at` on both [AB1]. Same content, same `at`: the larger `by` (w3hmxd) is kept as written, no question [X1, AQ2].

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ3: rent changed only on the phone: the phone's version, no question
cases.why: The desktop's rent is the one both last synced; only the phone changed it. Taken, nothing asked [AQ3].

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ3: rent changed on both devices: the person picks; until then the newer shows and both are kept
cases.why: Phone: rent up to 85,000 from 1 Dec (08:00). Desktop: renamed "Rent (flat)" (20:00). The same record, changed on both: one question. Shown meanwhile: the newer, the desktop's. `kept:<rent>` holds both versions, so whichever is picked the other stays for Undo [AQ3]. No field-by-field merge (that is stage 2, AQ5). AW6: the phone added a step, the desktop renamed it: different fields, so "keep both" is offered too (Rent (flat) with the 85,000 step).

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ3: the same change made on both devices asks nothing
cases.why: Both added 85,000 from 1 Dec. Apart from `at` and `by` the two versions are the same: one record, the newer (desktop), no question.

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ3, U: removed on the phone, renamed on the desktop: asked; the removal is kept as a version
cases.why: A removal is an edit (`gone`, a new `at`). Removed on one device and renamed on the other: asked. The rename is newer, so it shows; the removal waits in `kept:` and the person can still pick it.

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ3: two different fields of `home` changed on two devices: both kept, nothing asked
cases.why: Each field of `home` is its own settings item with its own `at` [AL1]: the country (phone) and the minimum (desktop) are two items, each changed on one device only.

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ3: the same `home` field changed on both devices: asked, `kept:home.main`
cases.why: The minimum set to 20,000 on the phone and 25,000 on the desktop: one item, two values. The newer (25,000) shows; both are kept; asked. A field value has no `told`, so the kept record is told at its earliest version (08:00).

cases.question: sync_symmetric
cases.title: AQ6: joining mine with theirs gives the same as theirs with mine (sy-12)
cases.why: The shown version is picked by `at`, then `gone`, then `by`, never by which side is "mine"; the kept versions are listed by `at`. So the join is the same from either side [AQ6].

cases.question: sync_again
cases.title: AQ6: joining again changes nothing (sy-12)
cases.why: With M the joined copy: M joined with itself is M; M joined again with either device's copy on the old base is M (the kept versions are the same two, the question the same one) [AQ6].

cases.question: answer
cases.title: AQ3: the person picks the phone's version: written as a new edit; both versions stay kept
cases.why: Picking version 0 (the phone's, 85,000 from 1 Dec) writes it as the record with a new `at` (09:00, the D4 clock: later than 20:00 seen) and `by`; `told` stays. The question is answered (`ask: false`, same `at`), and both versions stay in `kept:` [AQ3].

cases.question: answer
cases.title: AQ3: Undo of the pick brings the other version back
cases.why: Undo picks the other kept version (the desktop's rename): written with a new `at` (10:00). Nothing was lost by the first pick [AQ3].

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ3: the two devices answered the same question differently while offline: asked again
cases.why: Both synced the question (base M). The phone picked its own version at 09:00, the desktop picked its own at 12:00: rent changed on both to different content, so it is asked again. The kept versions are one per content, each its newest instance (the picks, 09:00 and 12:00), and the newer pick shows meanwhile.

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AP4 under AQ: a new pay day (bonus moved) on the phone and the bonus raised on the desktop: one question, nothing moved silently
cases.why: mg-271's story: the phone sets the new job's pay day (the 10th from 15 Dec) and moves the 25 Dec bonus to 10 Jan [AJ5]; the desktop raises the 25 Dec bonus to 450,000. One record changed on both: one question. The shown version (desktop, newer) is whole and sound: the 25th rule and its 450,000 key, so no X8 question and no bonus counted twice (AO1, AP4 become this) [AQ3, AQ4].

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AP2, confirm_review_8 g: a yearly bill moved offline while the other device ticked it: asked, never refused
cases.why: Desktop ticks the car insurance on 31 May 2027. The phone, offline, moved it to 15 Jun from 1 May. After the sync the change no longer makes 31 May, which is settled: X8 fails, and it is a question [AQ4, AP2]. AW3 (correcting AT2): a rule that is not monthly or weekly is offered from the day after the old rule's next occurrence after the last settled one: the old rule's next is 31 May 2028, so the offer is 1 Jun 2028 and the first new payment 15 Jun 2028. Nothing is paid twice in a year.

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AP2: a quarterly bill (`months`) moved offline while the other device ticked it
cases.why: Every 3 months on the 5th from 5 Dec: 5 Mar is due and the desktop ticks it. The phone moved it to the 20th from 1 Mar: 5 Mar is not one of its days. Asked [AQ4]. AW3: the old rule's next after 5 Mar is 5 Jun, so the offer is 6 Jun and the new rule's first day from it 20 Jun 2027 (not 20 Mar, two weeks after paying).

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AP2: a twice-a-year bonus (`monthsList`) changed offline while the other device ticked June
cases.why: June and December on the 10th; the desktop ticks 10 Jun 2027. The phone changed it to July and December from 1 Jun: 10 Jun is not made. Asked [AQ4]. AW3: the old rule's next after 10 Jun is 10 Dec 2027, so the offer is 11 Dec 2027; the new rule's first day from it is 10 Jul 2028 (not 10 Jul 2027, a month after the June payment).

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AP2, confirm_review_8 f: the 25th changed to the last working day while the other device ticked 25 Dec
cases.why: The last working day of December 2026 is Thu 31 Dec (no holiday table in the saved copy: weekends only). 25 Dec is settled and not made: asked, offering 26 Dec; next 31 Dec.

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AP2, confirm_review_8 f: the last working day changed to the 25th while the other device ticked 31 Dec
cases.why: 31 Dec (the last working day) is settled; the change to the 25th from 1 Dec does not make it. Asked, offering 1 Jan; next 25 Jan.

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AP2: a one-off (`once`) moved offline while the other device ticked it
cases.why: A one-off on 14 Mar, moved to 20 Mar from 1 Mar on the phone; the desktop ticked 14 Mar. Asked, offering 15 Mar; next 20 Mar.

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AP2: every two weeks moved offline while the other device ticked one
cases.why: Fridays every two weeks from 13 Nov: 27 Nov, 11 Dec, 25 Dec. The phone moved it to every two weeks from 18 Dec (18 Dec, 1 Jan): 25 Dec is not made. Asked, offering 26 Dec; next 1 Jan.

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AP2: a change that still makes the ticked day asks nothing
cases.why: Changed to the 10th and the 25th from 1 Dec: 25 Dec is still made. Sound: no question.

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AN2 under AQ: the pay day moved offline while the other device ticked the pay
cases.why: AN2's own story (a bill here, the same for pay): the 25th moved to the 10th from 1 Dec, 25 Dec ticked on the other device. AN2 moved the change silently; under AQ4 it is a question with the same offer, 26 Dec.

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AQ4, E x D: a December bonus set on one device and the pay day moved on the other: asked
cases.why: Both edits are to the pay schedule (the bonus is a key on it): the same record changed on both, so one question. The shown version (the desktop's, newer) keeps the 25th and its bonus key, which is sound: no X8 question.

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AP1, confirm_review_8 a: lunch on the closing day, logged on the phone after the desktop closed the e-wallet: sound, nothing asked
cases.why: Lunch 700 at 09:00 from the e-wallet, logged on the phone at 21:00. At 10:00 the desktop typed the e-wallet's 7,300 (after lunch) and closed it, moving 7,300 out. The closing's check holds everything dated on or before the closing day, whatever its `told` [AP1], so the lunch is inside 7,300: 7,300 - 7,300 = 0, closed and empty. Before AP1 the lunch (told 21:00, after 10:00) came after the check: -700 and the look ahead threw.

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AP1, confirm_review_8 d: a line dated after the closing day reopens the account, with a notice
cases.why: A statement line dated 9 Jan, after the closing day (8 Jan). One reopen rule for the look ahead and the sync: any event or check dated after the closing day reopens the account, with a notice [AP1]. Money out or in alike (the look ahead reopened only for money in).

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AP1, confirm_review_8 e: a check typed into the closed account after its closing day reopens it
cases.why: A check of 500 dated 12 Jan, after the closing day: reopened, with the notice [AP1].

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AQ4: a second figure typed on the closing day leaves 700 in the closed account: asked, never thrown
cases.why: The phone, offline, typed 8,000 for the e-wallet at 11:00 on 8 Jan (a refund of 700 came in). The latest figure on the closing day is 8,000 (told 11:00, after 10:00); the closing moved 7,300: 8,000 - 7,300 = 700 left in a closed account. The one-device check fails, so it is a question: move the 700 out, or open the account again [AQ4, P6].

cases.question: answer_check
cases.title: AQ4: answering "open it again" clears the closing; nothing is left to ask
cases.why: Reopened as an edit (new `at` 09:00 on 9 Jan, `by` the phone). An open e-wallet may hold 700.

cases.question: answer_check
cases.title: AQ4: answering "move it out" writes a second closing transfer to the main bank
cases.why: The 700 moves to the main bank, dated the closing day, as the closing's next record `close:<e-wallet>:2` [S3]: 8,000 - 7,300 - 700 = 0.

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: AW4 (AT3), AP5 under AQ: the main bank changed on the phone while the desktop changed that bank's own minimum: one question
cases.why: The phone makes the second bank the main bank (its 20,000 moves into `home.main`, its own `minBank` cleared) [AN3]; the desktop, offline, sets that bank's `minBank` to 25,000. The account changed on both (a `which`), and the main bank now has a minimum in two places (the `minimum` check). Under AW4 (AT3) these are one question showing both changes; the person picks one device's view (`options`, by device), which answers both.

cases.question: answer_check
cases.title: AP5: answering "keep 25,000" puts it in `home.main` and clears the account's own
cases.why: The figure lives in one place again: `home.main` holds 25,000, the account's own is null, both written at 09:00 by the phone. The account question stays until answered (both versions kept).

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: X5 under AQ4: money to place placed on both devices: more than there is, asked
cases.why: pe-55's story: 100,000 to place; the phone puts it all in the trip at 12:00, the desktop all in the car at 12:03. Waiting: 100,000 - 100,000 - 100,000 = -100,000. X5 let the newer give way silently; under AQ4 it is a question, offering to undo the newer placing (12:03, the car) [AQ4, X5]. AW6: it also offers to undo the older placing instead (12:00, the trip), so either can give way.

cases.question: answer_check
cases.title: X5 under AQ4: answering "undo the newer" removes the car placing; nothing is left to ask
cases.why: The car placing is removed by `gone` with a new `at` (nothing deleted): Waiting 100,000 - 100,000 = 0.

cases.question: imp_ids
cases.title: AP3: each line of a statement gets an id built from what it is
cases.why: A line with the statement's own reference: `ref:` and the reference (a space and a slash written as %20 and %2F). Without one: date, amount, direction and its count among such lines in the statement: two 1,200 coffees on 5 Nov are `:1` and `:2`; a 1,200 refund that day is `in:1` [AP3].

cases.question: id_ok
cases.title: AP3, AQ3: an import id and a kept id are ids the sync accepts
cases.why: The two new forms are read by the one shared reader (rules/ids.js) [AJ1]: `imp:<account>:ref:<reference>` and `imp:<account>:<date>:<amount>:<in|out>:<n>`, and `kept:<record id or field path>`. A direction other than in or out, or an empty reference, is not an import id. The older forms still pass.

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AP3, confirm_review_8 item 3: the same card statement read on the phone and on the desktop: each line once
cases.why: The phone reads the November card PDF on the train (08:10), the desktop reads the same file that evening (21:00). Each line has the same built id on both, and the same content: three records, not six. Each keeps the newer `at` (the desktop's) and the first `told` (08:10) [AP3, AQ2]. Before AP3 every line counted twice.

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AP3, O1: the desktop matched a line to a coffee only it knew; the phone read the same statement: still one record each
cases.why: The desktop typed a 1,200 coffee on 5 Nov (not synced yet); its import matched the first 1,200 line to it: the typed line is `gone` (goneBy the line) and the line takes its `told` [O1]. The phone read the same statement and had nothing to match. Each line has the same content on both apart from `told`: one record each, with the earliest `told` (the coffee's, 12:30 on 5 Nov, for the matched line). The coffee changed only on the desktop, so its removal stands: 4,500 + 1,200 + 1,200, no double, nothing asked [AP3, AQ2].

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AP6: a check-in on each device: both kept
cases.why: A check-in is a record of what happened (its stretch, its checks, its settled ids; no filler ids, the filler is worked out [AP6]). Two check-ins, two ids: both kept.

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AW6, AP6: one check-in changed on both devices only in its settled list: joined, not asked
cases.why: The phone unticked the rent settle; the desktop ticked the pay too. The two differ only in `settled`, which the person cannot judge as lists of ids [AW6]: joined three ways against the base: rent removed (phone), pay added (desktop), leaving the pay. The newer `at` and `by`, the earliest `told`; nothing asked.

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AP6, U: a check-in undone on the phone, untouched on the desktop: the Undo stands
cases.why: Only the phone changed it (its Undo): taken, nothing asked.

cases.question: cat_key
cases.title: AP7: the shop key is 38.31's stmtNorm with `k:` in front
cases.why: stmtNorm: lowercased, digits and * and # removed, every other character that is not a letter a space, spaces collapsed, the first three words; one long word cut to 12 letters; nothing left is "?" [AP7, src/stmt.js]. So a branch number never makes a new key. `k:` stays in front, so no key is `__proto__` [AN7].

cases.question: cat_learn
cases.title: AP7: a person's lesson beats a moved value, which beats a reader's guess
cases.why: A reader's guess for Lawson does not write over the moved value; a moved value does not write over the person's Seven Eleven lesson; a moved value writes over the reader's Family Mart guess; the person's Lawson lesson writes over the moved value [AP7].

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AP7: a person's lesson and a reader's guess for one shop on two devices: the lesson stands, the guess is kept, nothing asked
cases.why: A guess is not the person's edit and never replaces a lesson [AN7, AP7]: the lesson shows though the guess is newer. The guess is still kept, not asked.

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ3: two lessons for one shop on two devices: asked
cases.why: Both are the person's own: the same item changed on both, asked; the newer shows.

cases.question: sync_check
cases.title: R: a backup restored on the phone meets the desktop's edit since: only what both touched is asked
cases.why: The restore stamps every record with a new `at` [AE5]: rent goes back to the backup's 80,000, Food is stamped as it was. The desktop raised Food to 35,000 since the last sync. Rent changed only on the phone: the restore stands (a restore really rolls back). Food changed on both: asked [AQ3].

cases.question: sync_device
cases.title: A: a desktop back after three weeks is refused, takes the latest first and asks nothing about what only the phone changed
cases.why: The desktop last synced revision 3; the phone wrote up to 9 in three weeks. The desktop's write on 3 cannot be accepted; it takes 9: rent changed only on the phone (taken), its own lunch joins, revision 10 [AQ1].

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ3, people: a person renamed on both devices: asked
cases.why: A settings record changed on both: asked, the newer shows.

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AQ3: a `ui` key changed on one device and a limit on the other: both, nothing asked
cases.why: Two items, each changed on one device only.

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AP3: the same line read from a mid-month CSV on the phone and from the month's PDF on the desktop: one record, nothing asked
cases.why: The phone read a CSV exported on 16 Nov (1 to 15 Nov); the desktop read the November PDF. The 5 Nov coffee has the same id from both files (`imp:<card>:2026-11-05:1200:out:1`: the count is within its own day, and a file holds whole days). An import line's `src` says which file it was read from, not what happened, so it is not content: one record, the newer (the PDF's), the first `told`, nothing asked [AP3, AQ2]. Without this every line read from a CSV on one device and a PDF on the other would be a question.

cases.question: sync_device
cases.title: AQ1: a device with nothing new, whose list holds the same records in another order, writes nothing
cases.why: The desktop wrote revision 3 with one new spend; its list happens to hold the two lunches in the other order. The phone changed nothing: it takes revision 3 and writes nothing. A list of records is a set by id, so its order is never a change [section 0]. (Before this, the phone wrote a revision 4 that changed nothing, and the two devices looked different: the fuzz's first failure.)

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AP6, R: a backup from before a check-in, restored on the phone: the check-in is removed on both devices
cases.why: The backup is older than the 30 Nov check-in, so the restore removes it (`gone`, the restore's new `at`) [AE5]. The desktop did not touch it since the last sync: the removal is taken, nothing asked; the check-in does not come back.

cases.question: sync_device
cases.title: AP6, A: a desktop back after three weeks with its own check-in: both check-ins kept
cases.why: Behind (3 against 9): it takes 9, both check-ins join by id, revision 10 [AQ1, AP6].

cases.question: race
cases.title: AW5: the phone took revision 2 and joined; the desktop wrote revision 3 first: the refused write retries from the copy it took
cases.why: The phone changed the trip offline (300,000). It takes revision 2 (the desktop's rent 82,000) and joins: rent 82,000, trip 300,000. Before its write lands, the desktop writes rent 85,000 (revision 3): the write on revision 2 is refused [AQ1]. AW5: the phone saves the joined copy with revision 2 as its base before pushing, so the retry joins against revision 2: rent changed only on the desktop since (85,000), the trip only on the phone (300,000). Nothing is asked; revision 4. With the older base kept, rent would look changed on both sides and the person would be asked about two edits he made himself on the desktop (sync_review_1 race.js).

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AW1: rent ticked and a coffee typed on the phone, the bank statement read on the desktop: matching runs again after the sync, each payment once
cases.why: The desktop's matching (6.4) settled rent with the 80,000 line; it never saw the phone's tick or coffee. After the join, 6.4 runs again between import lines and typed or `set:` records that came from the other device [AW1]: the same account and direction, the same amount, inside the bank's posting window (1 working day). The tick (27 Nov) meets the 80,000 line of 27 Nov, the coffee (28 Nov) the 1,200 line of 28 Nov. Each typed record is `gone`, `goneBy` its line, with the newer of the two `at` (the import's, 21:00 on 29 Nov, by the desktop); each line keeps the typed record's `told` [O1] and its `settles` (rent's line has its own). Money out of the bank: 80,000 + 1,200 = 81,200, not 162,400; rent is settled by one live record.

cases.question: sync_device
cases.title: AW2: a desktop set up on its own turns the cloud on: which whole copy to keep is asked; nothing is joined
cases.why: The desktop has its own data and no `sync.base`; the cloud holds the phone's copy. Joining them would make two banks, two pay schedules and two openings (800,000 instead of 400,000). AW2: it asks which whole copy to keep; the cloud's copy shows meanwhile (one bank, one pay, 400,000), and both whole copies wait in `keptVersions` (`kept:copy`), written to the cloud so either device can answer.

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AW6: the e-wallet closed on both devices with two closing amounts: the closing transfer is worked out again from the joined events, not asked
cases.why: The phone logged a 700 lunch and closed the e-wallet, moving 7,300 out; the desktop, not knowing the lunch, closed it moving 8,000. Neither figure can be judged by the person; the right one comes from the joined events [AW6]: 10,000 (opening) - 2,000 (6 Jan) - 700 (lunch, 8 Jan) = 7,300. `close:<account>` is written with 7,300, the newer `at` and `by` (the desktop's), the earliest `told`; both versions stay kept for Undo, not asked. The closed account then holds 7,300 - 7,300 = 0: no closing question.

cases.question: sync
cases.title: AW6: rent renamed on the phone and given a new amount from January on the desktop: asked, with "keep both" offered
cases.why: One record changed on both devices: asked, the newer shown, both kept [AQ3]. The two changed different fields (the phone `name`, the desktop `steps`, each entry with its own `at` and `by`), so AW6 also offers "keep both": the base with each device's changed fields, `Flat rent` with the 82,000 step from January, the newer `at` and `by`.

open.question: AQ3 names plan and settings records. An event (a ticked pay, a check-in, an import line) changed two different ways on the two devices: is that asked too?
open.ref_does: Asks, the same way (sy-09, sy-48): the newer shows and both versions are kept. Events changed on one side, or the same way on both, join with no question.
